objective: Produce the lab's first probability-of-constraint-violation number on a design case, using subset simulation over the coefficient and inflow uncertainty the lab has already characterised, and state honestly which surrogate the tail rests on
rationale: Customers ask for this number and the lab has never produced one; a search of the whole estate for rare-event, tail-probability, failure-probability or subset-simulation machinery returns exactly one hit and it is the strategy line asking for it. The reason to file it now is that the inputs exist and are measured. The bluff-body design study characterised the coefficient channel twice on the same body, first by ten one-at-a-time corner solves giving a drag band 4.90 percent wide, which is 19.2 times the numerical channel on that case, and then by a twenty-sample Latin-hypercube stage over three coefficients giving 4.15 percent, about 55 percent of the corner envelope, at 26.91 core-minutes against a 60 core-minute estimate. That is a design case with a scalar output, a characterised input distribution and a measured per-solve cost, which is everything a constraint-violation probability needs except the constraint and the estimator. The honesty constraint is the whole reason this item must be filed carefully rather than run quickly: a tail probability computed from a surrogate is only as good as the surrogate's tails, and the lab's own process surrogate is measured as roughly three times overconfident on held-out data and is quarantined for exactly that reason. So this item either rides the repaired process once that repair validates, or it runs the estimator directly on solver evaluations at a coarser probability level and says which it did. A number reported without that disclosure would be worse than no number, because it would look like the answer customers asked for while resting on bars the lab already knows are too narrow. Axis A: reading-kind, priced from the design case's own measured Latin-hypercube stage. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0.

cost_basis: measured on the design case it uses: the Latin-hypercube stage spent 26.91 core-min for 20 solves on that body, about 1.35 core-min per solve, so the direct-evaluation seed level for a subset-simulation chain plus its verification points comes to about 30 core-min at the same rank count; the estimator itself and every surrogate evaluation cost nothing, and the price deliberately excludes any deeper subset level, which would be filed separately once the first level's acceptance behaviour is measured
expected_knowledge_gain: Four separable outcomes. One: the probability comes out at a level the seed sample can support directly, and the lab has its first constraint-violation number with a stated estimator and no surrogate in the tail. Two: the probability is small enough to need subset levels, and the measured acceptance behaviour of the first level prices the rest honestly, which is the input the follow-on filing needs. Three: the number depends materially on which surrogate carries the tail, which is a finding about the surrogate rather than about the design and routes straight back to the calibration repair. Four: the constraint as written is either never violated or always violated over the characterised input range, which means the constraint is uninformative and the useful product is the threshold at which it becomes informative.
sequencing: Slow-burn, subordinate to the Ladder V queue under strategy rule 1. It has a soft dependency on the calibration repair: the surrogate-carried variant should not run before that repair validates, and the direct-evaluation variant can run without it.
gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Rare-event / tail probability: subset simulation basics -> PROOF: one "probability of constraint violation" number on a design case (customers ask exactly this).' Operationalised: one number, on a named design case, for a constraint stated before the estimator runs, reported with its estimator, its coefficient of variation, and an explicit statement of whether any part of the tail rests on a surrogate; if it does, the surrogate's own held-out calibration must be quoted next to the number, and a surrogate whose held-out standardised residuals are known to be too narrow disqualifies the number from being reported without that quotation. A probability reported without an uncertainty on itself, or with the surrogate provenance unstated, fails the clause.
